introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: ANSWER ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: ANSWER ALL 2 questions in this section. Section C: ANSWER 2 QUESTIONS OUT OF 3; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first two will be considered. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Cu = 64.0, Mg = 24.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 $\mathrm{cm^3}$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 $\mathrm{J\,g^{-1}\,{}^{\circ}C^{-1}}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^{\circ}\mathrm{C} = 273\ \mathrm{K}$.

questions.corrige_markdown: The mole is the **amount of substance that contains $6.02\times10^{23}$ particles** (Avogadro's number) of that substance: as many particles as there are atoms in 12 g of carbon-12. The mass of one mole of a substance in grams equals its relative atomic or molecular mass.

questions.enonce_markdown:
2.4g of magnesium react with excess dilute hydrochloric acid.

(i) How many moles of magnesium are present in 2.4g? *[1 mark]*

(ii) Calculate the volume of hydrogen gas evolved at room temperature and pressure when the 2.4g of magnesium completely react. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Relative atomic mass of Mg = 24.0.

(i) Moles of Mg $= \dfrac{2.4}{24.0} =$ **0.1 mol**.

(ii) Equation: $\mathrm{Mg + 2HCl \rightarrow MgCl_2 + H_2}$ (balanced: Mg 1, H 2, Cl 2 on both sides).

From the equation, 1 mol of Mg gives 1 mol of $\mathrm{H_2}$, so 0.1 mol of Mg gives 0.1 mol of $\mathrm{H_2}$.

Volume of $\mathrm{H_2}$ $= 0.1 \times 24000\ \mathrm{cm^3} =$ **2400 $\mathrm{cm^3}$** (2.4 dm$^3$) at r.t.p.

questions.enonce_markdown:
In the extraction of Iron, carbon monoxide is used to reduce haematite ($\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}$)

(i) Write an equation to show how the carbon monoxide is formed in the blast furnace *[1 mark]*

(ii) Write an equation for the reduction of haematite to Iron. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Coke burns in the hot air blast: $\mathrm{C + O_2 \rightarrow CO_2}$. Carbon dioxide is then reduced by more hot coke: $\mathrm{CO_2 + C \rightarrow 2CO}$ (the equation that gives carbon monoxide).

(ii) $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3 + 3CO \rightarrow 2Fe + 3CO_2}$

Check: left Fe 2, O 3 + 3 = 6, C 3; right Fe 2, C 3, O 6. Balanced. Haematite is reduced (loses oxygen) to iron.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the substance that is used to remove sandy impurities *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: **Limestone (calcium carbonate, $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$)**. It decomposes in the furnace, $\mathrm{CaCO_3 \rightarrow CaO + CO_2}$, and the calcium oxide combines with the sandy impurity (silicon dioxide) to form molten slag, calcium silicate: $\mathrm{CaO + SiO_2 \rightarrow CaSiO_3}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Give one use of iron in our homes. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Any one of: cooking pots and pans, nails, roofing sheets (galvanised iron), burglar-proof doors and window guards, gates, cutlery, tools such as cutlasses and hoes.
